在MD模拟中,槲皮素表现出最稳定的结合,并且在体外测试中显示出对rCedV-NiV-B-GFP感染的剂量依赖性抑制作用。槲皮素具有高选择性指数(>20.8),并且与抗坏血酸联合使用可增强中和效果。 [10.3390/ijms27188026]
当前证据表明,几种NiV疫苗候选物,如亚单位、病毒载体和mRNA平台,已从实验阶段进展到早期临床评估阶段。 [10.3389/fddsv.2026.1906594]
通过LIR-DP,我们识别了来自22种HVVs的166个蛋白质中的43个潜在LIR模体,并预测其中18个LIR具有功能性。 [10.1371/journal.ppat.1014607]

papers.title: Nipah virus in the era of global connectivity: molecular evolution, transmission risk, and preparedness strategies
papers.abstract: Nipah virus (NiV) is a highly pathogenic zoonotic RNA virus belonging to the genus Henipavirus within the family Paramyxoviridae, representing a continuing global health concern due to its high case fatality rate and potential for epidemic expansion in the era of increasing international connectivity. The virus demonstrates strong evolutionary adaptability driven by the absence of proofreading mechanisms during RNA replication, enabling genetic diversification that may influence host range, virulence, and transmission dynamics. Molecular pathogenesis of NiV is primarily mediated through interaction of viral glycoproteins with ephrin-B2 and ephrin-B3 receptors, facilitating host cell entry, endothelial damage, and neuroinvasion. Immune evasion facilitated by the action of accessory proteins encoded by the P gene (P, V, W, and C) acts to suppress innate antiviral immunity through the inhibition of interferon induction and JAK/STAT signaling. Human-to-human transmission of Nipah virus remains limited, with epidemiological evidence indicating basic reproduction numbers generally below unity; however, respiratory involvement and healthcare-associated exposure may enhance cluster outbreaks. Global travel, ecological disruption, and fragmented surveillance systems contribute to spillover risk, particularly in South and Southeast Asia where fruit bats of the genus Pteropus serve as natural reservoirs. Despite advances in vaccine technology, including subunit, viral vector, mRNA-based platforms, and monoclonal antibody therapies, no licensed prophylactic or therapeutic agent is currently available for human use. Global preparedness remains challenged by the scarcity of high-containment biosafety facilities, limited research funding, and absence of integrated One Health surveillance networks. Ethical considerations surrounding wildlife population control further complicate disease mitigation strategies. Emerging genomic surveillance, artificial intelligence-assisted predictive modeling, and regional data-sharing frameworks are essential for early detection and response. Strengthening molecular research on viral-host interactions and transmission determinants will be critical for preventing future Nipah virus outbreaks in an increasingly interconnected world.

papers.title_zh: 在日益全球互联的时代,尼帕病毒(尼帕病毒)的分子特性、传播风险及应对策略
papers.source_body_en: Nipah virus (NiV) is a highly pathogenic zoonotic RNA virus belonging to the genus Henipavirus within the family Paramyxoviridae, representing a continuing global health concern due to its high case fatality rate and potential for epidemic expansion in the era of increasing international connectivity. The virus demonstrates strong evolutionary adaptability driven by the absence of proofreading mechanisms during RNA replication, enabling genetic diversification that may influence host range, virulence, and transmission dynamics. Molecular pathogenesis of NiV is primarily mediated through interaction of viral glycoproteins with ephrin-B2 and ephrin-B3 receptors, facilitating host cell entry, endothelial damage, and neuroinvasion. Immune evasion facilitated by the action of accessory proteins encoded by the P gene (P, V, W, and C) acts to suppress innate antiviral immunity through the inhibition of interferon induction and JAK/STAT signaling. Human-to-human transmission of Nipah virus remains limited, with epidemiological evidence indicating basic reproduction numbers generally below unity; however, respiratory involvement and healthcare-associated exposure may enhance cluster outbreaks. Global travel, ecological disruption, and fragmented surveillance systems contribute to spillover risk, particularly in South and Southeast Asia where fruit bats of the genus Pteropus serve as natural reservoirs. Despite advances in vaccine technology, including subunit, viral vector, mRNA-based platforms, and monoclonal antibody therapies, no licensed prophylactic or therapeutic agent is currently available for human use. Global preparedness remains challenged by the scarcity of high-containment biosafety facilities, limited research funding, and absence of integrated One Health surveillance networks. Ethical considerations surrounding wildlife population control further complicate disease mitigation strategies. Emerging genomic surveillance, artificial intelligence-assisted predictive modeling, and regional data-sharing frameworks are essential for early detection and response. Strengthening molecular research on viral-host interactions and transmission determinants will be critical for preventing future Nipah virus outbreaks in an increasingly interconnected world.
papers.abstract_zh: 尼帕病毒(尼帕病毒)是一种高致病性的动物源性RNA病毒,属于副粘病毒科亨尼帕病毒属,由于其高致死率和在全球日益紧密的国际联系背景下可能引发流行病扩散的潜力,构成了持续的全球健康威胁。该病毒表现出强大的进化适应性,这是由于其在RNA复制过程中缺乏校对机制,从而导致遗传多样性,这可能影响宿主的传播范围、致病力以及传播的动态变化。尼帕病毒的分子传播主要通过病毒糖蛋白与ephrin-B2和ephrin-B3受体的相互作用介导,促进宿主细胞进入、内皮损伤和神经侵袭。由P基因编码的辅助蛋白(P、V、W和C)通过抑制干扰素诱导和JAK/STAT信号通路,有助于逃避免疫应答,从而抑制先天免疫应答。人类之间的传播传播仍受到限制,流行病学证据表明其基本繁殖数通常低于1;然而,呼吸道感染和医疗相关暴露可能会增强集群暴发。全球旅行、生态破坏以及分散的监测系统增加了跨物种溢出风险,尤其是在南亚和东南亚地区,该属果蝠的储存宿主果蝠(Pteropus)是自然的储存宿主。尽管在疫苗技术方面取得了进展,包括亚单位疫苗、病毒载体疫苗、基于mRNA的平台和单克隆抗体疗法,但目前尚无获批用于人类的预防或治疗药物。全球应对能力受到高安全等级生物安全设施稀缺、研究资金有限以及缺乏整合的One Health 监测网络的挑战。关于野生动物种群控制的伦理问题进一步复杂化了疾病防控策略。新兴的基因组监测、人工智能辅助的预测建模以及区域数据共享框架对于早期检测和响应至关重要。加强病毒与宿主相互作用的分子研究以及传播决定因素的研究,对于防止未来在全球互联世界中出现的尼帕病毒暴发具有关键意义。

papers.abstract: Nipah virus (NiV) is a highly pathogenic zoonotic member of the genus Henipavirus . Due to its high fatality rate and increasing evidence of human-to-human transmission, it remains a major global health concern. Since its first emergence during the Malaysian outbreak, NiV has caused repeated outbreaks across South and Southeast Asia, particularly in Bangladesh and India. The absence of licensed vaccines or specific antiviral therapies has intensified the need for global efforts toward vaccine development and outbreak preparedness. This review aims to provide a comprehensive overview of the current status of NiV vaccine research, with emphasis on recent advances in vaccine platforms in preclinical and clinical trials. Relevant literature related to NiV epidemiology, viral pathogenesis, immunobiology, and vaccine development was comprehensively reviewed to summarize current knowledge and recent advances in vaccine development. Major vaccine approaches critically evaluated for their immunogenicity and protective response in this study include recombinant soluble glycoprotein subunit vaccines, viral-vectored vaccines, mRNA-based vaccines, DNA vaccines, virus-like particles, and nanoparticle-based systems. Recent advances in immunoinformatic-guided multi-epitope vaccine design and rapid-response vaccine manufacturing strategies were also assessed in the context of emerging pandemic preparedness initiatives such as Coalition for Epidemic Preparedness Innovations (CEPI) “100 Days Mission”. Current evidence indicates that several NiV vaccine candidates, like subunit, viral-vectored, and mRNA-based platforms, have progressed from experimental to early-phase clinical evaluation. However, the absence of validated immune correlates of protection, limited outbreak predictability, difficulties in conventional efficacy trials, and antigenic variability pose major challenges in outbreak-prone regions. Overall, continued advances in translational vaccinology, computational vaccine design, and global preparedness may accelerate the development of NiV vaccines.

papers.abstract_zh: 尼帕病毒(NiV)是亨尼帕病毒属中一种高度致病性的人兽共患病病毒。由于其高死亡率以及越来越多的人与人之间传播的证据,它仍然是全球主要的健康问题。自马来西亚首次出现尼帕病毒以来,该病毒在南亚和东南亚地区反复暴发,特别是在孟加拉国和印度。目前尚无获批的疫苗或特定的治疗药物,这加剧了全球在疫苗研发和疫情应对方面努力的必要性。本综述旨在全面概述尼帕病毒疫苗研究的现状,特别强调近期在临床前和临床试验中疫苗平台的进展。本研究综合回顾了与尼帕病毒疫苗、病毒传播、免疫生物学以及疫苗研发相关的文献,以总结当前的知识和疫苗研发的最新进展。本研究中对主要疫苗策略进行了批判性评估,包括重组可溶性糖蛋白亚单位疫苗、病毒载体疫苗、mRNA 基础疫苗、DNA 疫苗、类病毒颗粒以及基于纳米颗粒的系统。此外,近期在免疫信息学指导下多表位疫苗设计以及快速响应疫苗制造策略方面的进展也在此背景下进行了评估,例如“100 天使命”计划。目前的证据表明,几种尼帕病毒疫苗候选产品,如亚单位疫苗、病毒载体疫苗和 mRNA 基础疫苗,已经从实验阶段进入早期临床评估。然而,在易发生疫情的地区,缺乏经过验证的保护性免疫指标、疫情预测的局限性、传统有效性试验的困难以及抗原变异仍然是疫苗研发的主要挑战。总体而言,继续推进转化疫苗学、计算疫苗设计以及全球准备工作的进展,可能会加快尼帕病毒疫苗的研发进程。

analysis_zh.scope_and_question: 尼帕病毒(NiV)是基因组为亨尼帕病毒的高致病性人畜共患病成员。本综述旨在提供NiV疫苗研究的全面概述,重点在于预临床和临床试验中的疫苗平台的最新进展。
analysis_zh.evidence_base_and_review_method: 对与NiV感染、病毒学、免疫生物学和疫苗开发相关的文献进行了全面回顾,以总结当前的知识和疫苗开发的最新进展。本研究中评估的主要疫苗方法包括重组可溶性糖蛋白亚单位疫苗、病毒载体疫苗、mRNA疫苗、DNA疫苗、病毒样颗粒和基于纳米颗粒的系统,这些方法在免疫原性和保护性反应方面进行了关键评价。
analysis_zh.consensus_and_key_conclusions: 当前证据表明,几种NiV疫苗候选物,如亚单位、病毒载体和mRNA平台,已从实验阶段进展到早期临床评估阶段。
analysis_zh.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: 缺乏验证的免疫保护相关性、有限的流行病预测性、传统功效试验的困难以及抗原变异性的存在在易发地区构成了重大挑战。
analysis_zh.research_and_practice_implications: 最近在免疫信息学引导的多表位疫苗设计和快速响应疫苗制造策略方面也进行了评估,特别是在诸如“100天使命”计划之类的新兴大流行准备倡议的背景下。总体而言,继续推进转化性疫苗学、计算疫苗设计和全球准备可能加速尼帕病毒疫苗的开发。

papers.title: Discovery of Quercetin as a Potential Entry Inhibitor of Nipah Virus: A Path Toward Antiviral Therapy
papers.abstract: Nipah virus (NiV) is a zoonotic virus that causes severe encephalitis and respiratory disease with a mortality rate often exceeding 70%. Currently, there are no licensed vaccines or therapeutics for NiV disease. This study aimed to identify and experimentally evaluate small-molecule inhibitors targeting the NiV-G (attachment) glycoprotein using integrated in silico and in vitro approaches. A high-throughput virtual screening of >215,000 compounds was conducted against the NiV-G glycoprotein, using docking and molecular dynamics (MD) simulations. The next potential candidates were evaluated using an established, BSL-2-compatible recombinant Cedar virus (rCedV)-based green fluorescent protein (GFP) reporter virus expressing the NiV-F (fusion) and G glycoproteins (rCedV-NiV-B-GFP). During MD simulations, quercetin demonstrated the most stable binding, maintaining a consistent RMSD (3.25 ± 0.3 Å). In vitro testing showed dose-dependent inhibition of rCedV-NiV-B-GFP infection. elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 本研究旨在利用整合的计算机模拟与体外实验方法,识别并评估针对NiV-G(结合)糖蛋白的小分子抑制剂,以应对目前尚无获批的疫苗或治疗药物用于尼帕病毒感染的问题。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 本研究采用整合的计算机模拟与体外实验方法,包括针对NiV-G糖蛋白进行的超过215,000种化合物的高通量虚拟筛选,以及使用符合BSL-2级别的重组 Cedar 病毒(rCedV)为基础的绿色荧光蛋白(GFP)报告病毒(表达NiV-F(融合)和G糖蛋白,即rCedV-NiV-B-GFP)进行评估。
elements_zh.methods: 本研究采用对接和分子动力学(MD)模拟进行计算机模拟筛选,并通过rCedV-NiV-B-GFP病毒进行体外测试,以评估潜在抑制剂,重点研究了槲皮素。
elements_zh.main_results: 在MD模拟中,槲皮素表现出最稳定的结合,并且在体外测试中显示出对rCedV-NiV-B-GFP感染的剂量依赖性抑制作用。槲皮素具有高选择性指数(>20.8),并且与抗坏血酸联合使用可增强中和效果。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 本研究将槲皮素解释为一种有前景的小分子抑制剂,可能通过与NiV-G在计算识别的ephrin-B2/B3结合界面处的稳定相互作用来抑制尼帕病毒的细胞感染。这些发现强调了将计算筛选与BSL-2级别的细胞基生物测定相结合的重要性,以加速尼帕病毒应对措施的发现。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 这些发现可能为尼帕病毒疾病的抗病毒药物治疗提供信息,可能通过使用槲皮素或其与抗坏血酸的组合来实现,也可能加速尼帕病毒应对措施的发现。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 本研究的局限性在于使用了符合BSL-2级别的病毒,且需要在更高生物安全级别的环境中进一步验证。由于研究为体外性质,且需要进一步的临床验证,其证据强度中等。

papers.source_body_en: Nipah virus (NiV) is a zoonotic virus that causes severe encephalitis and respiratory disease with a mortality rate often exceeding 70%. Currently, there are no licensed vaccines or therapeutics for NiV disease. This study aimed to identify and experimentally evaluate small-molecule inhibitors targeting the NiV-G (attachment) glycoprotein using integrated in silico and in vitro approaches. A high-throughput virtual screening of >215,000 compounds was conducted against the NiV-G glycoprotein, using docking and molecular dynamics (MD) simulations. The next potential candidates were evaluated using an established, BSL-2-compatible recombinant Cedar virus (rCedV)-based green fluorescent protein (GFP) reporter virus expressing the NiV-F (fusion) and G glycoproteins (rCedV-NiV-B-GFP). During MD simulations, quercetin demonstrated the most stable binding, maintaining a consistent RMSD (3.25 ± 0.3 Å). In vitro testing showed dose-dependent inhibition of rCedV-NiV-B-GFP infection. Although quercetin alone was less potent (IC50 = 24 μM; 95% CI: 7.6–93.6 μM) than a reference NiV-neutralizing monoclonal antibody mAb-7B7 (IC50 = 0.027 μg/mL; approximately 0.00018 μM; 95% CI: 0.0108 to 0.0735), combination with ascorbic acid enhanced neutralization (IC50 = 4.4 μM; 95% CI: 2.9–6.8 μM). Quercetin demonstrated a high Selectivity Index of >20.8. The study identifies quercetin as a promising small-molecule inhibitor of NiV cellular infection, potentially through a stable interaction with NiV-G at the ephrin-B2/B3 binding interface identified computationally. These findings highlight the importance of combining computational screening with BSL-2 cell-based bioassays to accelerate NiV countermeasure discovery.
papers.abstract_zh: 尼帕病毒(尼帕病毒,NiV)是一种人兽共患病病毒,可引起严重的脑炎和呼吸系统疾病,其死亡率率通常超过70%。目前尚无获批的疫苗或治疗药物用于尼帕病毒感染。本研究旨在利用整合的计算机模拟与体外实验方法,识别并评估针对NiV-G(结合)糖蛋白的小分子抑制剂。进行了对超过215,000种化合物的高通量虚拟筛选,针对NiV-G糖蛋白进行对接和分子动力学(MD)模拟。接下来,通过一种已建立的、符合BSL-2级别的重组 Cedar 病毒(rCedV)为基础的绿色荧光蛋白(GFP)报告病毒(表达NiV-F(融合)和G糖蛋白,即rCedV-NiV-B-GFP)评估潜在候选药物。在MD模拟中,槲皮素表现出最稳定的结合,其RMSD保持在3.25 ± 0.3 Å。体外测试显示槲皮素对rCedV-NiV-B-GFP感染具有剂量依赖性抑制作用。尽管单独使用槲皮素的抑制效果(IC50 = 24 μM;95% CI: 7.6–93.6 μM)不如参考的尼帕病毒中和单克隆抗体mAb-7B7(IC50 = 0.027 μg/mL;约0.00018 μM;95% CI: 0.0108至0.0735),但与抗坏血酸联合使用可增强中和效果(IC50 = 4.4 μM;95% CI: 2.9–6.8 μM)。槲皮素表现出高选择性指数(>20.8)。本研究识别槲皮素为一种有前景的小分子抑制剂,可能通过与NiV-G在计算识别的ephrin-B2/B3结合界面处的稳定相互作用来抑制尼帕病毒的细胞感染。这些发现强调了将计算筛选与BSL-2级别的细胞基生物测定相结合的重要性,以加速尼帕病毒应对措施的发现。
papers.summary_zh: 尼帕病毒(尼帕病毒,NiV)是一种人兽共患病病毒,可引起严重的脑炎和呼吸系统疾病,其死亡率率通常超过70%。目前尚无获批的疫苗或治疗药物用于尼帕病毒感染。本研究旨在利用整合的计算机模拟与体外实验方法,识别并评估针对NiV-G(结合)糖蛋白的小分子抑制剂。进行了对超过215,000种化合物的高通量虚拟筛选,针对NiV-G糖蛋白进行对接和分子动力学(MD)模拟。接下来,通过一种已建立的、符合BSL-2级别的重组 Cedar 病毒(rCedV)为基础的绿色荧光蛋白(GFP)报告病毒(表达NiV-F(融合)和G糖蛋白,即rCedV-NiV-B-GFP)评估潜在候选药物。在MD模拟中,槲皮素表现出最稳定的结合,其RMSD保持在3.25 ± 0.3 Å。体外测试显示槲皮素对rCedV-NiV-B-GFP感染具有剂量依赖性抑制作用。尽管单独使用槲皮素的抑制效果(IC50 = 24 μM;95% CI: 7.6–93.6 μM)不如参考的尼帕病毒中和单克隆抗体mAb-7B7(IC50 = 0.027 μg/mL;约0.00018 μM;95% CI: 0.0108至0.0735),但与抗坏血酸联合使用可增强中和效果(IC50 = 4.4 μM;95% CI: 2.9–6.8 μM)。槲皮素表现出高选择性指数(>20.8)。本研究识别槲皮素为一种有前景的小分子抑制剂,可能通过与NiV-G在计算识别的ephrin-B2/B3结合界面处的稳定相互作用来抑制尼帕病毒的细胞感染。这些发现强调了将计算筛选与BSL-2级别的细胞基生物测定相结合的重要性,以加速尼帕病毒应对措施的发现。

analysis_zh.research_question_and_background: 本研究旨在利用整合的计算机模拟与体外实验方法,识别并评估针对NiV-G(结合)糖蛋白的小分子抑制剂,以应对目前尚无获批的疫苗或治疗药物用于尼帕病毒感染的问题。
analysis_zh.study_design_and_population: 本研究采用整合的计算机模拟与体外实验方法,包括针对NiV-G糖蛋白进行的超过215,000种化合物的高通量虚拟筛选,以及使用符合BSL-2级别的重组 Cedar 病毒(rCedV)为基础的绿色荧光蛋白(GFP)报告病毒(表达NiV-F(融合)和G糖蛋白,即rCedV-NiV-B-GFP)进行评估。
analysis_zh.methods: 本研究采用对接和分子动力学(MD)模拟进行计算机模拟筛选,并通过rCedV-NiV-B-GFP病毒进行体外测试,以评估潜在抑制剂,重点研究了槲皮素。
analysis_zh.main_results: 在MD模拟中,槲皮素表现出最稳定的结合,并且在体外测试中显示出对rCedV-NiV-B-GFP感染的剂量依赖性抑制作用。槲皮素具有高选择性指数(>20.8),并且与抗坏血酸联合使用可增强中和效果。
analysis_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 本研究将槲皮素解释为一种有前景的小分子抑制剂,可能通过与NiV-G在计算识别的ephrin-B2/B3结合界面处的稳定相互作用来抑制尼帕病毒的细胞感染。这些发现强调了将计算筛选与BSL-2级别的细胞基生物测定相结合的重要性,以加速尼帕病毒应对措施的发现。
analysis_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 这些发现可能为尼帕病毒疾病的抗病毒药物治疗提供信息,可能通过使用槲皮素或其与抗坏血酸的组合来实现,也可能加速尼帕病毒应对措施的发现。
analysis_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 本研究的局限性在于使用了符合BSL-2级别的病毒,且需要在更高生物安全级别的环境中进一步验证。由于研究为体外性质,且需要进一步的临床验证,其证据强度中等。

papers.title: Discovering host-viral protein interactions in autophagy: A LIR discovery pipeline for identifying LC3-interacting region motifs in highly virulent viruses
papers.abstract: Hemorrhagic fever virus (HFV) infections are highly fatal, posing a significant global pandemic threat as they continue to emerge in new locations. HFVs and other highly virulent viruses (HVVs), such as Nipah virus, exploit host cell pathways, including the conserved host autophagy pathway, to promote viral replication. The Atg8/microtubule-associated protein 1 light chain 3 (LC3) proteins are necessary for autophagosome formation and maturation. Proteins interact with Atg8-family proteins through LC3-interacting region (LIR) motifs, which is a short linear motif (SLiM) found in intrinsically disordered regions of proteins. The presence of these motifs in viral components suggests they play a role in hijacking or evading the host autophagy pathway, yet the identification of functional LIR motifs in viral proteins remains limited. news.title: Machine learning accelerates drug repurposing against Nipah virus with computational validation - Bioengineer.org
news.rss_summary_html: Machine learning accelerates drug repurposing against Nipah virus with computational validation  Bioengineer.org
news.excerpt_original: Machine learning accelerates drug repurposing against Nipah virus with computational validation Bioengineer.org
news.priority_tier_reason: 可信机构来源或已成功抓获正文
news.content_title: Machine learning accelerates drug repurposing against Nipah virus with
news.content: The Nipah virus, one of the deadliest pathogens on the World Health Organization’s priority list, has long haunted public health officials across South and Southeast Asia. With case fatality rates that can exceed 70 percent, no licensed antiviral therapy, and outbreaks that erupt unpredictably in Bangladesh, India and Malaysia, the virus represents one of the most daunting challenges in modern virology. Now, researchers at the ICMR-National Institute of Virology in Pune, India, have turned to artificial intelligence to close the therapeutic gap, deploying machine learning models to sift through thousands of existing drugs and identify compounds that could be repurposed against the virus. The study, published in the journal Molecular Diversity, describes a computational pipeline that trained algorithms on known Nipah inhibitors, screened a library of more than 9,000 compounds, and validated the most promising candidates through molecular docking and molecular dynamics simulations. Led by Shivangi Sharma, with Pragya D. Yadav and Sarah Cherian as senior authors, the research team assembled a training dataset of 211 compounds drawn from three publicly curated sources: the Anti-Nipah database, the Nipah Virus Inhibitor Knowledgebase (NVIK), and PubChem, supplemented by a systematic review of the literature. This dataset contained both known inhibitors and inactive compounds, providing the labeled examples needed for supervised learning. Each molecule was converted into a numerical fingerprint using molecular descriptors calculated with the Mordred software, capturing features such as molecular weight, topological indices, electronic properties and atom-type electrotopological states. These descriptors serve as the language through which algorithms perceive chemical structure, allowing a model to learn which patterns of atoms, bonds and charge distributions correlate with antiviral activity against Nipah virus. The investigators benchmarked seven different supervised machine learning algorithms: Support Vector Machines, Random Forest, Logistic Regression, Decision Tree, k-Nearest Neighbors, Artificial Neural Networks, and Ridge Classifier. Each was trained and evaluated using standard performance metrics, including accuracy, receiver operating characteristic analysis, and the Matthews correlation coefficient, a measure favored in cheminformatics because it remains robust even when classes are imbalanced. Among all seven, the Random Forest model, an ensemble method that aggregates the votes of hundreds of decision trees each trained on random subsets of the data, emerged as the clear winner. analysis_zh.scale_impact_and_risk: 该研究识别了八种候选分子,包括已知化合物如2,3,4,5,6-五没食子酰葡萄糖、乙基没食子酸和帕里欣A,这些化合物可能被重新用于尼帕病毒的治疗。未报告确诊病例或死亡病例。
analysis_zh.response_status_and_uncertainty: 该研究正处于调查和测试阶段,通过计算验证、分子对接以及动力学模拟等方法识别潜在抑制剂。目前研究结果尚未在临床试验中得到确认。

Goran Bajic, PhD, and Raianna Fantin, PhD, researchers in the Department of Microbiology at the Icahn School of Medicine at Mount Sinai, are two of four early- and mid-career scientists selected through a competitive international application process. Each fellow will receive three years of funding to advance research on new treatments for emerging infectious diseases. The Cumming Global Centre for Pandemic Therapeutics in Melbourne, Australia, established the program to support the next generation of pandemic therapeutics researchers and strengthen international collaboration and preparedness for future health threats. Goran Bajic, PhD: Broadly Protective Antibodies Against Henipaviruses Dr. Bajic will investigate broadly protective antibody therapies against henipaviruses, including Nipah and Hendra viruses, which can cause severe and often deadly outbreaks. His mentor, Benhur Lee, MD, Ward-Coleman Chair in Microbiology, Icahn School of Medicine at Mount Sinai, will support the work. Dr. Bajic will develop nanoparticles that display proteins from multiple henipaviruses to generate fully human antibodies and smaller, adaptable nanobodies designed to block multiple viral strains. The project will combine virology and structural biology to identify promising antibody candidates and determine how they interact with henipaviruses. The goal is to develop antibody-based therapies that provide broader protection against known and emerging henipaviruses and reveal viral vulnerabilities that could inform future treatments. “Henipaviruses represent a significant pandemic threat, and there are currently no approved vaccines or broadly effective antibody treatments,” said Dr. Bajic. “This fellowship will allow us to explore new approaches for developing antibody therapeutics that could provide protection across multiple henipaviruses and, ultimately, help us respond more rapidly when new viral threats emerge.” Raianna Fantin, PhD: Advancing Monoclonal Antibody Countermeasures for Orthopoxviruses Dr. Fantin will focus on developing a potential antibody treatment for mpox, an ongoing global public health threat for which improved therapeutic options are needed. Supported by her mentor, Camila Coelho, PhD, Assistant Professor of Microbiology at the Icahn School of Medicine, Dr. Fantin will advance EV35-6, a human monoclonal antibody that targets a conserved viral protein involved in the systemic spread of mpox. Previous research has shown that EV35-6 can protect mice from mpox infection when administered before or after infection. Through the fellowship, Dr. Fantin will evaluate EV35-6 in nonhuman primates, examining therapeutic effectiveness, safety, persistence in the body, route of administration, and distribution across tissues. The findings are intended to provide evidence needed to advance EV35-6 toward clinical development. “The opportunity to move a promising antibody treatment for mpox closer to clinical development is incredibly exciting,” said Dr. Fantin. “This support will enable us to address important questions about how the antibody works in a more clinically relevant model and help determine whether it has the potential to become a therapeutic option for patients.” The Cumming Global Fellows Program combines research funding with leadership development based on the adaptive leadership framework developed by Ron Heifetz, MD, MPA, and Martin Linsky, JD. Fellows participate in annual leadership immersions, workshops, and interactive learning experiences designed to build skills for leading complex, multidisciplinary efforts to address global health challenges. The inaugural cohort will begin the fellowship program in September 2026. “The selection of Drs. Bajic and Fantin reflects Mount Sinai’s leadership in developing innovative approaches to emerging and re-emerging pathogens and our longstanding commitment to infectious disease research,” said Ana Fernandez-Sesma, PhD, Chair of the Department of Microbiology at the Icahn School of Medicine. “Their projects also underscore the importance of advancing therapeutics before the next pandemic emerges, rather than waiting until an outbreak is underway.” About the Icahn School of Medicine at Mount Sinai The Icahn School of Medicine at Mount Sinai is internationally renowned for its outstanding research, educational, and clinical care programs. It is the sole academic partner for the seven member hospitals* of the Mount Sinai Health System, one of the largest academic health systems in the United States, providing care to New York City’s large and diverse patient population. The Icahn School of Medicine at Mount Sinai offers highly competitive MD, PhD, MD-PhD, and master’s degree programs, with enrollment of more than 1,200 students. It has the largest graduate medical education program in the country, with more than 2,700 clinical residents and fellows training throughout the Health System. The Graduate School of Biomedical Sciences offers 12 degree-granting programs, conducts innovative basic and translational research, and trains more than 470 postdoctoral research fellows. Ranked 11th nationwide in National Institutes of Health (NIH) funding, the Icahn School of Medicine at Mount Sinai is among the 90th percentile of U.S. private medical schools in Sponsored Programs Direct Expenditures per Principal Investigator, according to the Association of American Medical Colleges. More than 6,900 scientists, educators, and clinicians work within and across dozens of academic departments and multidisciplinary institutes with an emphasis on translational research and therapeutics. Through Mount Sinai Innovation Partners (MSIP), the Health System facilitates the real-world application and commercialization of medical breakthroughs made at Mount Sinai. ------------------------------------------------------- * Mount Sinai Health System member hospitals: The Mount Sinai Hospital; Mount Sinai Brooklyn; Mount Sinai Morningside; Mount Sinai Queens; Mount Sinai South Nassau; Mount Sinai West; and New York Eye and Ear Infirmary of Mount Sinai. Tags: Icahn School of Medicine at Mount Sinai, Infectious Diseases, Goran Bajic, PhD, RAIANNA FANTIN, Ana Fernandez-Sesma, PhD, Mount Sinai Health System, Research About the Mount Sinai Health System Mount Sinai Health System is one of the nation’s leading integrated academic health systems and one of the largest in the New York metropolitan area. Its comprehensive system includes seven hospitals, more than 400 outpatient practices, over 600 research and clinical laboratories, the Icahn School of Medicine at Mount Sinai, the Graduate School of Biomedical Sciences, and the Mount Sinai Phillips School of Nursing. Together, the Health System comprises approximately 48,000 employees, more than 9,000 physicians, and 8,600 nurses. As a leading learning health system, Mount Sinai combines clinical expertise with scientific discovery to improve patient care while training the next generation of health care and biomedical leaders. The Health System provides care across every stage of life, from prenatal care through geriatrics, while advancing personalized medicine through artificial intelligence, data science, and biomedical research. Mount Sinai is consistently recognized among the nation’s leading academic health systems for patient care, research, and education. The Mount Sinai Hospital is ranked No. 1 in New York by Newsweek and No. 5 on the magazine’s World’s Best Hospitals list. The Icahn School of Medicine at Mount Sinai ranks No. 11 among U.S. medical schools and No. 1 among freestanding medical schools for National Institutes of Health funding, reflecting the strength of its scientific enterprise and leadership in biomedical research. close× close× Original text Rate this translation Your feedback will be used to help improve Google Translate Language 1 Language 2 Language 3 We use cookies and similar technologies to improve your experience, analyze usage, and deliver relevant content or ads. Goran Bajic, PhD, and Raianna Fantin, PhD, researchers in the Department of Microbiology at the Icahn School of Medicine at Mount Sinai, are two of four early- and mid-career scientists selected through a competitive international application process. Each fellow will receive three years of funding to advance research on new treatments for emerging infectious diseases. The Cumming Global Centre for Pandemic Therapeutics in Melbourne, Australia, established the program to support the next generation of pandemic therapeutics researchers and strengthen international collaboration and preparedness for future health threats. Goran Bajic, PhD: Broadly Protective Antibodies Against Henipaviruses Dr. Bajic will investigate broadly protective antibody therapies against henipaviruses, including Nipah and Hendra viruses, which can cause severe and often deadly outbreaks. His mentor, Benhur Lee, MD, Ward-Coleman Chair in Microbiology, Icahn School of Medicine at Mount Sinai, will support the work. Dr. Bajic will develop nanoparticles that display proteins from multiple henipaviruses to generate fully human antibodies and smaller, adaptable nanobodies designed to block multiple viral strains. The project will combine virology and structural biology to identify promising antibody candidates and determine how they interact with henipaviruses. The goal is to develop antibody-based therapies that provide broader protection against known and emerging henipaviruses and reveal viral vulnerabilities that could inform future treatments. “Henipaviruses represent a significant pandemic threat, and there are currently no approved vaccines or broadly effective antibody treatments,” said Dr. Bajic. “This fellowship will allow us to explore new approaches for developing antibody therapeutics that could provide protection across multiple henipaviruses and, ultimately, help us respond more rapidly when new viral threats emerge.” Raianna Fantin, PhD: Advancing Monoclonal Antibody Countermeasures for Orthopoxviruses Dr. Fantin will focus on developing a potential antibody treatment for mpox, an ongoing global public health threat for which improved therapeutic options are needed. Supported by her mentor, Camila Coelho, PhD, Assistant Professor of Microbiology at the Icahn School of Medicine, Dr. Fantin will advance EV35-6, a human monoclonal antibody that targets a conserved viral protein involved in the systemic spread of mpox. Previous research has shown that EV35-6 can protect mice from mpox infection when administered before or after infection. Through the fellowship, Dr. Fantin will evaluate EV35-6 in nonhuman primates, examining therapeutic effectiveness, safety, persistence in the body, route of administration, and distribution across tissues. The findings are intended to provide evidence needed to advance EV35-6 toward clinical development. “The opportunity to move a promising antibody treatment for mpox closer to clinical development is incredibly exciting,” said Dr. Fantin. “This support will enable us to address important questions about how the antibody works in a more clinically relevant model and help determine whether it has the potential to become a therapeutic option for patients.” The Cumming Global Fellows Program combines research funding with leadership development based on the adaptive leadership framework developed by Ron Heifetz, MD, MPA, and Martin Linsky, JD. Fellows participate in annual leadership immersions, workshops, and interactive learning experiences designed to build skills for leading complex, multidisciplinary efforts to address global health challenges. The inaugural cohort will begin the fellowship program in September 2026. “The selection of Drs. Bajic and Fantin reflects Mount Sinai’s leadership in developing innovative approaches to emerging and re-emerging pathogens and our longstanding commitment to infectious disease research,” said Ana Fernandez-Sesma, PhD, Chair of the Department of Microbiology at the Icahn School of Medicine. “Their projects also underscore the importance of advancing therapeutics before the next pandemic emerges, rather than waiting until an outbreak is underway.” About the Icahn School of Medicine at Mount Sinai The Icahn School of Medicine at Mount Sinai is internationally renowned for its outstanding research, educational, and clinical care programs. It is the sole academic partner for the seven member hospitals* of the Mount Sinai Health System, one of the largest academic health systems in the United States, providing care to New York City’s large and diverse patient population. The Icahn School of Medicine at Mount Sinai offers highly competitive MD, PhD, MD-PhD, and master’s degree programs, with enrollment of more than 1,200 students. It has the largest graduate medical education program in the country, with more than 2,700 clinical residents and fellows training throughout the Health System. The Graduate School of Biomedical Sciences offers 12 degree-granting programs, conducts innovative basic and translational research, and trains more than 470 postdoctoral research fellows. Ranked 11th nationwide in National Institutes of Health (NIH) funding, the Icahn School of Medicine at Mount Sinai is among the 90th percentile of U.S. private medical schools in Sponsored Programs Direct Expenditures per Principal Investigator, according to the Association of American Medical Colleges. More than 6,900 scientists, educators, and clinicians work within and across dozens of academic departments and multidisciplinary institutes with an emphasis on translational research and therapeutics. Through Mount Sinai Innovation Partners (MSIP), the Health System facilitates the real-world application and commercialization of medical breakthroughs made at Mount Sinai. ------------------------------------------------------- * Mount Sinai Health System member hospitals: The Mount Sinai Hospital; Mount Sinai Brooklyn; Mount Sinai Morningside; Mount Sinai Queens; Mount Sinai South Nassau; Mount Sinai West; and New York Eye and Ear Infirmary of Mount Sinai.
